ALGER — Le ministère des Postes et Téléc: ALGIERS — The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications announces a gradual generalization of the IPv6 protocol in Algeria. This technology, successor to IPv4, must meet the growing needs for IP addresses and improve the quality of digital services.
Une transition technologique majeure pou: A major technological transition for the telecoms sector
Le ministère des Postes et Télécommunica: The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications is launching an awareness and training campaign among players in the sector to promote the adoption of the IPv6 protocol. This initiative is part of the modernization of the country's internet infrastructure. According to the authorities, IPv6 will make it possible to lift the current limits linked to the shortage of IP addresses available under IPv4, while offering superior performance in terms of throughput and latency.
Le protocole IPv6, standardisé depuis 19: The IPv6 protocol, standardized since 1998, is already deployed in several wilayas of the country. National telecom operators, including Algérie Télécom, Mobilis, Djezzy and Ooredoo, are called upon to accelerate their migration. A test phase was successfully carried out in certain public infrastructures, confirming the technical feasibility of this transition.
Des sessions de formation sont organisée: Training sessions are organized across the national territory to familiarize engineers and technicians with the specificities of IPv6. These workshops target network administrators in wilayas, daïras and municipalities, as well as those responsible for critical infrastructure. The ministry emphasizes the importance of this transition to secure data exchanges and guarantee optimal interoperability with international networks.
Des avantages multiples pour l'écosystèm: Multiple benefits for the digital ecosystem
L'adoption de l'IPv6 est présentée comme: The adoption of IPv6 is presented as a solution to current challenges, including the saturation of IPv4 addresses and the exponential growth of connected objects. The authorities emphasize that this technology will also allow better management of internet traffic, a reduction in operational costs and an improvement in the quality of service for end users.
